page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on external storage options, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the CPU performance of the ecs.c4.4xlarge in the average tier. The stress-ng single-core test scored 1578.98, while the multi-core test reached 16657.34. In data processing tasks, the instance achieved a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 77.01 GB/sec and a static web serving throughput of 9.51 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning workloads, the server processed 135M parameter LLM prompts at 991.37 tokens/sec and generated text at 169.31 tokens/sec.

A key tradeoff of this instance is its memory subsystem performance. While the CPU capabilities are solid, the PassMark memory score of 1797.16 is categorized in the bottom 25%, indicating a potential bottleneck for memory-intensive operations. However, the dedicated core allocation and Intel Xeon architecture provide stable compute density. This makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or high-speed local storage.

The hardware profile and benchmark results indicate that the ecs.c4.4xlarge is suitable for compute-heavy workloads such as web serving, batch processing, data decompression, and lightweight model inference. It is also applicable for database operations that fit within its 32.0 GB memory limit.
